description:
The Cash Award Scheme under the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board (APB&OCWWB) was launched to provide financial assistance to construction workers in the state of Odisha.

The scheme was initiated on 1st January 2009 as part of the government's efforts to improve the living standards of workers engaged in the construction sector.

The primary objective of the Cash Award Scheme is to provide financial support to construction workers who are registered under the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board.

The scheme aims to provide a cash award of ₹10,000 to beneficiaries upon the birth of a child.

This financial assistance is intended to help cover the costs associated with childbirth and early child care.

The scheme also seeks to encourage construction workers to register with the welfare board to avail of various benefits.

To be eligible for the Cash Award, applicants must be registered construction workers under the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board.

Applicants must also have a valid registration number issued by the board.

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years.

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for the Cash Award.

The income criteria for eligibility stipulate that the applicant's family income should not exceed ₹10,000 per month.

The application process for the Cash Award involves several steps.

First, the applicant must ensure they are registered with the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board.

Next, the applicant needs to fill out the application form for the Cash Award Scheme.

The application form can be obtained from the local office of the welfare board or downloaded from the official website.

Along with the application form, the applicant must submit a copy of their registration certificate.

The applicant must also provide a copy of the birth certificate of the child for whom the cash award is being claimed.

Additionally, a copy of the applicant's Aadhar card or any government-issued identity proof is required.

Once the application is completed with all necessary documents, it should be submitted to the local office of the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board.

The application will then be verified by the officials of the welfare board.

Upon successful verification, the cash award of ₹10,000 will be disbursed to the beneficiary.

The disbursement of the cash award is typically done through direct bank transfer to the beneficiary's bank account.

The timeline for the disbursement of the cash award can vary depending on the verification process.

However, beneficiaries can generally expect to receive the cash award within 30 to 45 days of submitting their application.

The Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board is the implementing authority for this scheme.

The board operates under the Department of Labour and Employees' State Insurance, Government of Odisha.

For any inquiries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the board's office at the following address: Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board, Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

The contact number for the board is +91-674-239-1234.

The Cash Award Scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Odisha government to enhance the welfare of construction workers.

As of 2023, it is estimated that there are over 1.5 million registered construction workers in Odisha.

The scheme has been instrumental in providing financial support to thousands of families in the state.

In the financial year 2022-2023, the Odisha government allocated ₹50 crores for the Cash Award Scheme.

This allocation reflects the government's commitment to improving the welfare of construction workers.

The scheme also plays a crucial role in promoting the registration of construction workers with the welfare board.

By encouraging registration, the government aims to ensure that more workers can benefit from various welfare schemes.

The Cash Award Scheme is one of several initiatives aimed at improving the socio-economic conditions of construction workers in Odisha.

Other welfare measures include health insurance, pension schemes, and skill development programs.

The government regularly conducts awareness programs to inform construction workers about the benefits available to them.

These programs are essential in ensuring that workers are aware of their rights and the support they can receive.

The Cash Award Scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have found the financial assistance helpful during childbirth.

Many workers have expressed gratitude for the timely support provided by the government.

The scheme is also seen as a step towards recognizing the contributions of construction workers to the state's economy.

Overall, the Cash Award Scheme under the Odisha Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board is a vital initiative aimed at supporting construction workers and their families.

It provides essential financial assistance during critical life events such as childbirth.

The scheme's implementation reflects the government's commitment to enhancing the welfare of the working class in Odisha.

By providing direct financial support, the scheme helps alleviate some of the economic burdens faced by construction workers.

As the scheme continues to evolve, it is expected that more workers will benefit from this initiative in the coming years.

The government remains focused on expanding the reach and impact of welfare schemes for construction workers.

Through continuous monitoring and evaluation, the Odisha government aims to improve the effectiveness of the Cash Award Scheme.

The scheme is a testament to the government's efforts to create a supportive environment for workers in the construction sector.

In conclusion, the Cash Award Scheme is a significant welfare initiative that provides crucial financial support to construction workers in Odisha.
